newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power ends higher on cash, San Onofre news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power ends higher on cash, San Onofre news.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Monday on stronger physical prices in the West and news that restart of the San Onofre 3 nuclear power unit in California was delayed.
August Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 75 cents at $35.10 a megawatt hour (MWh) after a session low at $34.00.
September PV finished up 70 cents at $29.26. Deferred PV ended up five to 35 cents.
August California-Oregon Border (COB) settled up 14 cents after bouncing between $22.90-23.35.
September COB finished up six cents at $22.88. Other active COB months ended flat to down 15 cents.

Day-ahead electricity prices for Tuesday at PV surged to $31.00-35.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from $26.50-28.00 Thursday amid options-related buying, while PV's strength spilled over to COB which rose 50 cents to $17.00-18.00.

Southern California Edison Co (SoCal Edison) said it delayed the restart of its 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 3 nuclear unit by a week to July 17. Engineers needed time to replace the unit's instrument nozzles.
The unit, in San Clemente, Calif., has been offline since April 12 for refueling and maintenance.
SoCal Edison added the adjacent 1,080 MW unit 2 is still on scheduled to return to service about July 10 afte being shut Jne 29 to replace its charge line check valves.
Brokers and traders said today's rise will likely be short-lived due to seasonal weather in the West and more generation, both coal and nuclear, coming back to service.
"You still have the other San Onofre unit as well as the Diablo Canyon (unit 2) coming back," a Houston trader said.

PG&E Corp's 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear power unit on the central California coast reached 50 percent power Monday and was expected to hold at that level until midday before resuming power ascension.

The unit on the central California coast restarted from a July 2 shutdown due to problems with its feedwater system. The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was in a startup mode as of early today but had not yet reconnected to the electricity grid.

Almost 2,500 MW of coal-fired generation in the West was scheduled to resume production by today, including two 670 MW Centralia units in Washington, 330 MW Colstrip units in Montana, a 260 MW Hayden unit in Colorado and a 550 MW Laramie River unit in Wyoming.
Meteorlogists called for wet and cool weather in the Northwest this week before a warming trend early next week.
Meanwhile, readings are forecast to run near normal over most of the Southwest but below normal in the far northeast region and above normal in the extreme southwest area.
NYMEX estimated 877 PV and 338 COB contracts were sold.
